messages:
morgan: heads-up — noticed repeated TPM spikes in eu-west during last deploy, queue depth shot up and we hit the per-customer RPM guardrails
raj: when you say "TPM spikes" — is that per-instance accounting or aggregate cluster tokens?
morgan: aggregate. the admission controller kept allowing small bursts that depleted credits; then regen kicked in and we got a big wave of queued requests catching up
sierra: can you paste the metric traces? latency vs token-consumption would help
morgan: here's a quick snapshot
```
metric: tpm_consumed_cluster_eu_west
peak: 12.8k TPM @ 2025-11-03T14:22Z
sustained: ~9k TPM for 3m
queue_len: 240 -> drained in 18s after regen
```
emma: hmm, that looks like token-bucket hysteresis problem. we're refilling too aggressively on short windows
opsbot: [auto] scaled pool eu-west-gpu from 16 -> 12 due to low allocation ratio
raj: two issues: burst credits size (bucket capacity) and the refill smoothing. right now refill is instantaneous per-minute slot
sierra: proposal: add EWMA smoothing to the refill_rate and a small hysteresis window before raising admission thresholds. prevents cycle where regen -> flood -> throttle -> regen
morgan: +1. also consider separating short/long seq workloads. short chat calls consume tiny tokens but spike RPS; long-compute calls burn a lot but low RPS
emma: sketch of parameters I tested in staging:
```
base_refill = floor(GPU_capacity_tokens_per_min * 0.85)
bucket_size = max(2 * base_refill, min(8000, 0.1 * cluster_peak))
ewma_alpha = 0.2  # 5-step smoothing
hysteresis_pct = 0.06  # 6% before scaling up/down
```
result: peak oscillation reduced by ~40%, tail latency down 15%
raj: good start. need to account for region cross-routing — when eu-west saturates we route to eu-central; that bursts the other pool unless we include reserved headroom
sierra: we should add a small reserved headroom token pool per-region (e.g., 5% of capacity) strictly for emergency reroutes. tracked and billed separately
morgan: cost question: reserving headroom increases idle cost. can we trade by preemptible GPUs for headroom to reduce cost?
emma: preemptible is ok for short reroutes but limits SLA. for Dedicated customers we must avoid preemptible fallback
raj: operationally: implement EWMA refill + hysteresis on controller flags. tweak bucket_size formula per-model since large-context models should have larger per-request tokens
sierra: add tests: simulate 20% surge of short seq traffic while simultaneously bringing 2 nodes down and measure drop rates
opsbot: [alert] queued requests > 200 for > 30s in eu-west — auto-notify
morgan: I'll open a PR with the EWMA + hysteresis change and a config toggle. will include the staging numbers and simulation script
emma: thanks. once PR is up ping the perf-test channel, i'll run the surge scenarios
raj: quick note on formula docs in PR: include worked examples. e.g. for a 16-GPU pool with model A:
```
GPU_capacity_tokens_per_min = 16 * 2000 = 32000 tokens/min (model-cost adjusted)
base_refill = floor(32000 * 0.85) = 27200 tokens/min
bucket_size = max(2 * 27200, 8000) = 54400
hysteresis window +/- 6% = ~1632 tokens
```
sierra: nice. also include telemetry spans for when hysteresis prevents a scale action — useful for postmortem if we ever mis-tune
morgan: will do. PR later today, target staging deploy tomorrow morning
emma: :thumbsup:
raj: thanks all — let's iterate on numbers after we have staging results
opsbot: [info] PR morgan/ingest/ewma-hysteresis created: https://git.internal/r/morgan/ingest/pull/412
